title: Tenant Segmentation Incident: Evidence Handling & Forensic Guidance
author: Marta Ruiz
body:
Summary:

This page defines the operational runbook and evidence-handling guidance for incidents that impact tenant segmentation or authorization boundaries in Redwood Inference (hosted and dedicated modes). It ties together RBAC containment procedures, audit log capture, cross-region data residency considerations, secure-SDLC remediation requirements, and compliance evidence packaging for regulatory review. Intended audience: Security on-call, SRE, platform engineers, privacy/compliance, and legal.

Goals and scope:
- Contain and isolate affected tenant(s) within 30 minutes of detection for high-impact incidents (see "Severity rubric" below).
- Capture forensically-sound evidence from compute, network, and storage while preserving data residency constraints.
- Produce a packaged evidence artifact suitable for internal RCA and regulator audits within 72 hours.
- Ensure remediation steps are coordinated with release/control gates in the secure SDLC so fixes do not regress production controls.

Terminology:
- Tenant segmentation incident: any event where a tenant's data, requests, or metadata are accessible to another tenant or to unauthorized principals due to an authorization, routing, or configuration failure.
- Evidence artifact: a reproducible bundle of logs, KV snapshots, configurations, and attestations required for investigation and audit.

Severity rubric (examples):
1) Sev1 (Critical): confirmed cross-tenant data exposure (PII or customer-authenticated responses) or broad authorization bypass affecting >10 customers. SLA: contain within 30 min, notify legal and CRO.
2) Sev2 (High): suspected segmentation flaw with limited blast radius (1–10 customers) or authorization misconfiguration that may allow access, not yet confirmed. SLA: contain within 2 hours.
3) Sev3 (Medium): RBAC policy drift or audit-log gaps with no confirmed exposure. SLA: investigate within 24 hours and remediate in next sprint or hotfix depending on impact.

Immediate containment checklist (ordered, numbered):
1) Triage and declare incident severity. Owner: security-oncall. Use PagerDuty group: sec-oncall-tenant.
2) Apply immediate routing policy to redirect affected tenant traffic to safe-handling tier (redwood-routing CLI):
   - Example: redwood-routing set-policy --tenant-id t-012345 --policy isolate --duration 3h
3) Revoke short-lived credentials for affected tenants and for implicated service accounts. Commands:
   - aws sts revoke-sessions --user-id <id> (for AWS SSO: script in /infra-scripts/revoke-sessions.sh)
   - k8s: kubectl delete secret <secret-name> -n <tenant-namespace>
4) If running on Dedicated or Private deployments, escalate to customer infra contact per customer runbook and notify via secure channel (IdP group + encrypted email).

Forensic evidence capture (preservation-first principles):
- Preserve before edit. Never modify disk images, configuration files, or primary audit stores in-place unless required for containment; prefer copies.
- Tag each artifact with an immutable evidence ID and timestamp (UTC). Example format: EVID-<YYYYMMDD>-<service>-<short-hash>.

Required evidence items (minimum):
- Compute snapshot or process list covering the incident window (ps aux, container images list).
- Kernel and application logs: journalctl -u redwood-runtime --since "2026-02-10T10:00:00Z" > runtime.log
- Auth events and policy evaluations from the ABAC/RBAC engine (authz-audit service). Query example (internal logging):
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $LOG_API_KEY" "https://log-api.internal/v1/search?q=tenant:t-012345 AND event:authz_eval&from=2026-02-10T09:50:00Z&to=2026-02-10T10:20:00Z" > authz-events.json
- KV cache snapshots (when applicable) with redaction markers if required by privacy policy. Use redwood-kvctl snapshot --tenant t-012345 --out kv-snapshot.tar.gz
- Network captures limited to headers where full packet capture would violate data residency/PII constraints; when full PCAP is required and allowed, capture using tcpdump -w and store in controlled evidence bucket.

Evidence packaging and metadata table (required fields):
| field | description | example |
| EVID_ID | Unique artifact id | EVID-20260210-authz-9f3a |
| SEVERITY | Declared severity | Sev1 |
| TENANTS | Affected tenants | t-012345, t-078901 |
| REGIONS | Regions where data origin/routing occurred | us-east-1, eu-west-1 |
| DATA_RESIDENCY | Residency constraints | EU_ONLY |
| ARTIFACTS | List of files included | runtime.log, authz-events.json, kv-snapshot.tar.gz |
| HASHES | SHA256 hashes for each artifact | sha256:... |

Storage, encryption, and retention controls for evidence artifacts:
- Evidence artifacts MUST be uploaded to the evidence S3 bucket: s3://redwood-evidence-prod. Use server-side encryption with KMS: --sse aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111122223333:key/abcd-efg.
- For cross-border incidents, use a region-locked bucket mirroring strategy: write-only replication to s3://redwood-evidence-eu for EU-data, with explicit legal hold tag: "legal_hold=true".
- Retention policy applied: evidence-retention=7 years for Sev1, 2 years for Sev2, 6 months for Sev3. See retention config file example:

Retention policy JSON example:
{
  "evidenceBucket": "redwood-evidence-prod",
  "retentionBySeverity": {"Sev1": "2555d", "Sev2": "730d", "Sev3": "180d"},
  "kmsKey": "arn:aws:kms:..."
}

RBAC and auth telemetry required for investigation:
- authz-audit service: full policy evaluation logs and policy-version metadata.
- IAM entitlement change logs (user-provisioning, role-assignments) from entitlement-service.
- OAuth/OIDC token minting logs (token issuance and revocation).
- Admin console session recordings (redwood-admin-activity) limited to metadata per privacy rules.

Data residency and cross-border constraints:
- If the incident involves EU-only tenants (residency label present), evidence must remain in EU zone buckets and access must be granted only to staff with EU processing authorization. See label: residency:EU.
- For hybrid-residency customers, coordinate with Privacy & Legal before any artifact transfer outside permitted zones.

Chain-of-evidence steps (recommended):
1) Assign evidence custodian: security investigator (primary) and SRE (secondary).
2) Create evidence record in internal tracker: evidence-id, artifacts list, custodian, custody log.
3) Collect artifacts using read-only copies and compute SHA256 hashes.
4) Upload to evidence bucket with encryption and immutability flags (if supported).
5) Update custody log with date/time, operator, action, and destination URI.

Secure-SDLC integration and remediation gating:
- All code changes intended to remediate segmentation incidents must pass an elevated review: security-review required + automated policy tests for RBAC regression.
- Pull request checklist additions for remediation PRs:
  - unit/regression tests covering the RBAC policy paths
  - canary rollout plan with feature flag and fallback
  - performance backstop to ensure latency SLOs not violated (99th percentile token latency must remain within baseline + 30%).
- Release blocking criteria: failing evidence-preservation steps or incomplete audit captures are release-blocking until resolved.

Notifications and stakeholders (communication):
- Pager duty groups: sec-oncall-tenant, platform-oncall.
- Slack channels (restricted): #sec-tenant-incidents (read-only for non-stakeholders).
- Notification cadence: initial triage within 15 minutes for Sev1 to legal, C-level ops; hourly updates until containment.

Regulatory and compliance packaging (what to provide to auditors):
- Evidence manifest (CSV) with artifact URIs, hashes, custodian signatures, residency assertions, and legal hold tags.
- Signed preservation affidavit from custodian describing actions taken and timing. Template available as /templates/preservation-affidavit.md.
- Redacted sample of impacted request/response pairs with consistent redaction rules documented in /security/redaction-guidelines.md.

Operational templates and automation (location):
- Collection scripts: /infra-scripts/evidence-collector.sh (invoked with --evid-id).
- Custody tracker template: internal jira template 'EVID-TRACKER'.
- S3 lifecycle and replication manifests: terraform modules under infra/terraform/modules/evidence-buckets.

Post-incident review and risk/exceptions handling:
1) Within 7 days: post-incident review (owner: security manager) with attendees: SRE, product, legal, affected OEMs/customers as needed.
2) Document root cause, sequence-of-events, and permanent remediations in the RCA page.
3) If remediation requires an exception to existing controls (temporary entitlements, expanded cross-region access), file a risk-and-exceptions request using the template at /confluence/security-and-compliance/risk-and-exceptions/exception-request-template. The request must include compensating controls and an explicit expiration time.

Monitoring and regression detection after remediation:
- Add continuous evals to detect recurring policy overrides: daily authz-audit queries for anomalous policy evaluations.
- Include synthetic tests in the perf suite that simulate tenant boundary checks (see eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite/tenant-isolation-tests).

Appendix A — Example commands and snippets:
- Export authz events: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $LOG_API_KEY" "https://log-api.internal/v1/stream?tenant=t-012345&service=authz-audit&from=2026-02-10T09:50:00Z" | jq . > authz-stream.ndjson
- Snapshot KV store (GCP datastore example): gcloud datastore export --kinds=redwood_kv --namespaces=t-012345 gs://temp-evidence/kv-export-20260210
- Evidence upload (AWS example): aws s3 cp authz-events.json s3://redwood-evidence-prod/evid/EVID-20260210-authz-9f3a/ --sse aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111122223333:key/abcd-efg

Appendix B — Ownership and contact matrix:
- Security-oncall: PagerDuty sec-oncall-tenant, primary investigator.
- SRE: platform-oncall, assists with snapshots, network captures, and kube-level containment.
- Privacy & Legal: consult for residency, cross-border transfer, and regulatory notifications.
- Customer Success: coordinates customer communication for Dedicated and Private deployments.
